title: PO Acceptance Pack
purpose: A short, fixed PO acceptance check for user clarity, product intent and understandable end-to-end behavior. Technical regression evidence remains owned by automated authorities and is not replayed manually.

policy.scope_rule: Every P0 scenario in the functional acceptance matrix with manual_po_acceptance=true must be represented exactly once in this pack.

journeys.title: First use, onboarding and settings
journeys.purpose: Judge whether a new household can get into the product, understand its configuration and return to it without product knowledge.
steps: Open the product as a new user, register and sign in.
Complete onboarding for one household and choose the location setting that best fits the test household.
From the resulting home screen, open Settings and change the location setting once.
Return to the normal user flow and confirm that navigation and visible choices match the changed setting.
Sign out and sign in again, then confirm that the active household and its configuration are understandable.
acceptance_criteria: The user always knows what the next meaningful action is.
Labels and explanations are understandable without implementation knowledge.
The location setting has an obvious and consistent effect on visible product choices.
Signing out and back in does not create uncertainty about the active household or configuration.

journeys.title: Household collaboration and permission boundaries
journeys.purpose: Judge whether invitations, household context and role boundaries are understandable to normal users.
steps: As a household administrator, invite a second user.
Accept the invitation as the second user and open the household.
Switch household context when more than one household is available and confirm that the active context is obvious.
As the non-administrator, attempt one household setting that is intentionally restricted.
Return to normal household use and judge whether the restriction and current role remain understandable.
acceptance_criteria: Invitation and acceptance language makes the relationship between user and household clear.
The active household is visually and conceptually unambiguous.
A restricted action produces an understandable product response rather than a technical error.
Nothing in the interface suggests access to another household's data or administrator privileges.

journeys.title: Receipt to stock and almost-out journey
journeys.purpose: Judge the core product story from receipt review through unpacking and stock management without replaying technical edge-case tests.
steps: Upload one normal supported receipt and review it in Kassa.
Approve the receipt and continue to Uitpakken for a small representative subset of its articles.
Assign the visible choices that a normal user would make and finish unpacking those articles.
Open Voorraad and inspect one processed article, its current stock and its visible history.
Perform one normal consumption action so the article becomes relevant for Bijna op, then open Bijna op.
Open two distinct article details, rename one of them and confirm that the other still feels like a separate article in detail and history.
acceptance_criteria: Kassa, Uitpakken, Voorraad and Bijna op feel like one coherent user journey rather than separate technical modules.
The product gives enough feedback to understand what has been accepted, processed and changed.
Stock and almost-out behavior is understandable from the user's actions without knowing internal calculations.
Article detail and history remain conceptually tied to the article the user selected, including after a rename.
No technical terminology or internal identifiers are required to understand the journey.

journeys.title: Platform administration without household privilege confusion
journeys.purpose: Judge whether platform administration communicates its separate authority model clearly and safely.
steps: Open the platform administration area with a role that is allowed to use it.
Inspect the available administration functions and the way platform context is presented.
Perform one safe permitted administration action available in the test environment.
Return to household context and confirm that platform authority is not presented as household membership or household administrator access.
acceptance_criteria: Platform context is visibly distinct from normal household use.
Permitted and unavailable actions make sense for the signed-in platform role.
The interface does not imply that a platform role silently grants household privileges.
The administration action gives clear product feedback.

execution_policy.overall_acceptance_rule: accepted only when every required journey is accepted and there are no blocking findings
execution_policy.evidence_boundary: The PO records verdicts and concise product observations only. Automated test evidence remains the responsibility of the technical release authorities.
